hits.hook: Scott Hanselman: Emma Marie Cryer (OpenRouter) - think cost per task, not cost per token; a cheap model that can't finish can waste more
hits.text:
The mistake Emma Marie Cryer sees all the time is thinking about cost per token instead of cost per task. A cheap model that can't finish the job can waste more than a frontier model.

Emma is at OpenRouter.

Full episode: https://t.co/DX1KmXUrFP https://t.co/DYNIgk46y8
hits.original:
The mistake Emma Marie Cryer sees all the time is thinking about cost per token instead of cost per task. A cheap model that can't finish the job can waste more than a frontier model.

Emma is at OpenRouter.

Full episode: https://t.co/DX1KmXUrFP https://t.co/DYNIgk46y8
hits.draft_en:
Emma Marie Cryer on Scott Hanselman's show: stop thinking cost per token. Think cost per task.

A cheap model that can't finish the job isn't cheap. It's a retry loop with a nice invoice.

Same rule for agent budgets. Measure what one finished task costs. Then pick the model.
hits.video_tip: Vertical 8s: two receipts side by side, a short one labelled 'per token' and a long curling one labelled 'retries'. You tear off the long one. Caption: 'Cost per task.'

drafts.rides: @shanselman cost per task, not per token (13K) + @github Copilot Fusion 30% off (78K) + your Outlook meeting-cost star (now 27.8K)
drafts.text:
Emma Marie Cryer on Scott Hanselman's show: stop thinking cost per token. Think cost per task.

A cheap model that can't finish the job isn't cheap. It's a retry loop with a nice invoice.

Same rule for agent budgets. Measure what one finished task costs. Then pick the model.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 8s: two receipts side by side, a short one labelled 'per token' and a long curling one labelled 'retries'. You tear off the long one. Caption: 'Cost per task.'

drafts.rides: @burkeholland Copilot removed an <hr> (9.3K, question post) + @code agents keep working while you step away (25K)
drafts.text:
Burke Holland just had GitHub Copilot remove one <hr>.

That's the real adoption curve. Not the big demo. The day a one-line edit stops being worth your own keystrokes.

What's the smallest thing you handed to Copilot this week?
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 6s: zoomed screen recording of a single horizontal line disappearing from a page after a Copilot prompt. Caption: 'Adoption looks like this.'

drafts.rides: @sama Private Inference testing (1.31M) + @gdb confidential computing for prompts and responses (109K)
drafts.text:
OpenAI is testing Private Inference with a small group of customers. Confidential computing, strict controls over prompts and responses while the model processes them.

Most enterprise AI conversations hit the same wall: where does the prompt go?

Privacy isn't a feature request. It's the gate before production.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 8s: a paper labelled 'prompt' slides into a locked box, the box shuts with a click. Caption: 'Where does the prompt go?'

drafts.rides: @code latest release - no sleep while agents work, isolated Dev Containers (25K) + @simonw 194 agent co-authored commits (29K)
drafts.text:
The latest VS Code release can keep your machine awake while agents work.

We have officially entered the "don't close the lid, the intern is busy" era.

The better part: agent sessions can run in isolated Dev Containers. Let it work. Just not on your whole machine.
drafts.video_tip: Vertical 6s: your hand goes to close a laptop, a sticky note on the screen reads 'agent working, do not close'. You back away slowly. Caption: 'The intern is busy.'

drafts.rides: @sama Thanksgiving note (251K) + your error-code screenshot post + Thanksgiving-week quiet on the watchlist
drafts.text:
Happy Thanksgiving to my friends in the US.

Thankful this year for: test questions, approval steps, spending caps, and everyone who leaves the error code in the screenshot.

Canada did turkey in October, so I'm on agent watch today.
